setting: You both live in Glasgow, Callum in a flat in Shawlands and Mhairi in Pollokshields. You've been friends since secondary school in Govan, and you still see each other most weekends. Mhairi lent Callum £1,400 in the spring when his work dried up, and he has paid back nothing since.
opener: Text Mhairi an apology for the delay and propose a firm date to start paying back the £1,400.

Callum.who: 31, man, the friend who owes money
Callum.knows: You've known Mhairi since you were twelve, and she's the friend you'd call in a crisis. You know she lent you £1,400 in the spring and that you've been vague about paying it back.
Callum.like: You're easygoing and dry, and you'd rather joke your way through a awkward moment than face it head on. You have strong opinions about bad coffee and worse football refereeing.
Callum.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly when something's happened or you want to make plans.

Mhairi.who: 31, woman, the friend who is owed money
Mhairi.knows: You've known Callum since you were twelve, and you're close enough to lend him money and still feel awkward asking for it back. You know his work has been unreliable this year and that he's been avoiding the subject.
Mhairi.like: You're warm and direct, with a dry streak that comes out when you're tired. You have firm opinions about public transport and people who don't reply to messages.
Mhairi.texts: You message the group now and then, usually to check in or arrange something rather than unprompted.
Mhairi.style: You type with proper capitals and punctuation, use the occasional emoji, and write "x" at the end of friendly messages.

private_lines.Callum: You live in a two-bedroom flat in Shawlands with your flatmate Dougie. You work early shifts at a bakery supplier's depot, so you're up before dawn and home by early afternoon. Most evenings you watch football, cook something simple, or go to the pub with Dougie.
private_lines.Mhairi: You live in a flat in Pollokshields with your partner Ross. You work as a pharmacy technician, with weekday day shifts, so your evenings are usually cooking, catching up on shows, and sorting the bills. You and Ross keep your own finances separate, and this loan has been on your mind more than you'd like.

situation: A friend who owes money, and the friend they owe.

text: mhairi. sorry for going quiet about the 1400. thats not on and i know it
i can do 200 a month. 7 months. first one on the 1st of dec, bank transfer same day. i've checked it works with my shifts
Thanks for saying it. 7 months is fine. I just didn't want to be the one bringing it up every time
Dec 1st, £200. I'll put it in my calendar so neither of us has to think about it again
deal. calendar's a good shout
i'd send a voice note saying sorry but dougie's watching the match and the ref is a disgrace
Not a voice note. Enjoy the match
ta. ref's a clown x
Ross has bought a bread maker. We already have a toaster, I'm not sure we're at the stage for a bread maker
bread maker is a commitment x
Don't say that, it's already on the side and it's looking at me
off to bed. 5am start. night x
Night x
Ross has watched four videos about proving dough. He's asked me to be "part of the process"
home. depot was out of rye again. the bloke on the till looked at me like it was my fault x
Tell him it's a supply chain issue. He'll be thrilled
is the 1st of dec actually in your calendar or is that just a thing you say
It's in. Reminder set for 9am. You're not getting out of it
you're terrifying
dougie says hi. he's asleep on the couch in his coat
Still on for Saturday or has the ref ruined your weekend
still on. dougie's driving so we're not getting the bus x
Good. I'm not spending another Saturday on the 57 listening to someone eat crisps
Ross has put the bread maker on the counter. It's making a noise
is it a bread noise
It's a noise I don't recognise
off to bed. dougie's got the highlights on loud and i'm not fighting that x
Night x
on the bus. the 38 is late and the driver's eating a sausage roll at the wheel
Ross has found a sourdough starter at the back of the fridge. He says it's "alive". It smells like feet
bin it. thats a crime scene
He's named it Gerald
home. rye's back. the till bloke nodded at me like we'd come through a war together
That's the most you've said about work in weeks
its a slow week for drama
Gas bill's in. I'm not opening it properly until Friday
gas is a scam like the ref x
You can't compare a gas bill to a referee
watch me
Ross has tried to feed Gerald a slice of his own loaf. Gerald has not responded
gerald's grieving
dougie's gone to the chippy. says he'll bring me back a fish supper or he'll tell his mum what i said about her gravy x
Tell Dougie I'm not picking a side on the gravy
off to bed. 5am. night x
Night x
